newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.N. arms chief Richard Butler said in Manama Baghdad recognised it was time to complete the process of eliminating weapons of mass destruction. The ball was now in Iraq's court, he said.

- Embassies in Bahrain have urged citizens staying illegally in the Gulf Arab state to take advantage of a government amnesty to leave the country or legalise their stay without punishment before October 31.
- Advertising agencies in the Gulf say it was unclear how a Gulf-wide ban on television and radio advertising of cigarettes and tobacco products would affect indirect advertising.
- Sharjah International Airport said work would begin "very soon" to increase the length of its runway by 250 metres (0.16 miles) from a current 400 metres (0.25 miles).
- Foreign assets with the Central Bank of Oman shot up by 25.7 percent in the first four months of 1997 to 894.2 million rials compared with the year-ago period.
- Abu Dhabi has begun a 155 million dirham project to construct 150 houses for low-income citizens.
- Sharjah-based Crescent Refining and Marketing Co Ltd's $650 million hydrocarbon project in Pakistan is back on track, company officials said on Sunday.
- Sharjah Airport's total cargo volumes in the first half of 1997 rose by more than 28 percent over the same period a year earlier.

- Dubai Investment has announced it was setting up the country's first private electricity plant at a cost of 120 million dirhams. Capacity in the first phase would be 60 megawatt, rising to 120 megawatt in the second phase.
- Dubai hotel investments until the year 2000 will reach 4.35 billion dirhams.
